correctness.rationale: For each two-colouring the red-degree vector gives nonzero adjacency eigenvector at eigenvalue 2-d. The exact rook spectrum excludes all parameter pairs except total size four or six. The zero-row-and-column eigenspace excludes both size-six exceptions. Explicit two- or three-colour boundary certificates are checked by finite exhaustive computation. All remaining parameters have degree at least five and hence three-colour upper by arXiv:2608.04122v1 Theorem 4; no indefinite computation is used as proof.

evidence: Pękała–Przybyło, arXiv:2608.04122v1, Theorem 4, establishes Maj-prime(G)<=3 whenever minimum degree is at least five.

Antoniuk–Prorok–Salia, arXiv:2607.00212v1, Introduction, notes a three-colour Euler-tour construction when the Eulerian graph has number of edges divisible by three; this covers the upper bound for R_{3,3}.
Neither theorem excludes two colours for all rook graphs, and the minimum-degree-five result does not apply to R_{2,4} or R_{3,3}.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broad upper-bound results cover a part of the proof and are expressly credited. They do not dominate the exact index classification; the new lower bound and outstanding degree-four boundary are material.

The published degree-at-least-five result is used explicitly as the three-colour upper bound, not passed off as a new theorem.
